evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: 字形分析; 甲骨文用例; 金文用例; 傳世文獻引申義
evidence.text: The database analyzes 門 as an image of two door leaves, sometimes with a lintel in oracle-bone forms. It reports oracle-bone uses for a gate, including ancestral-temple and hall gates, and a use as a place name. A bronze-inscription example uses it for a gate; the source also reports a verbal use meaning to attack a city gate and cites transmitted-text examples for extensions such as path or key point, and lineage or category. These are the database's analyses and reported examples; they do not establish the first occurrence of every later sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫—漢字甲骨部件分析：門

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: 甲骨、金文、戰國竹簡用例
evidence.text: Reports 《合集》32035, with 門 used for a gate at an ancestral temple; 《合集》30285 for a hall gate; the bronze inscription 格白𣪕 for passing through the east gate; and a Qin-slip example from 《睡虎地秦簡·法律答問》 in which 問 means to ask. These are dated text traditions or cited artifact corpora, not independent chronological proof of when each sense arose. The same entry cautions, for 問, that early graph forms resembling the later graph do not by themselves prove the represented word was already 'interrogate'.

evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫 (Academia Sinica Character Database)
evidence.text: The database indexes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and Small Seal forms, and describes 門 as formed from two 戶, resembling two opposing door leaves. It provides artifact/catalogue references including 集成03136. The webpage supplies no independently inspectable dates for each form in its text.
evidence.title: 漢字「門」：字形演變

evidence.source: 說文解字 entry reproduced by 說文解字在線查詢
evidence.field: 說文原文; 字形演變; 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The entry gives the Han-dynasty dictionary explanation 聞也。从二戶。象形 and lists oracle-bone, mid-Western-Zhou bronze, Chu, Qin slip, Western-Han, Eastern-Han, and seal-script examples. This records Xu Shen's historical analysis; it is not contemporary evidence for the graph's original formation. Duan Yucai's later note treats 聞 as a phonetic gloss (聲訓).
evidence.title: 「門」字的说文解字

evidence.text: The page calls 门 the simplified form of 門 and labels it a pictograph of a gate. Its graphic sequence labels oracle script approximately 1250–1000 BC, middle Western Zhou bronze script approximately 900 BC, Shuowen seal script approximately 100 AD, and Eastern Han clerical script 25–220 AD. These are the website's supplied labels; I did not inspect the linked glyph images, so I make no independent visual observation.
evidence.title: 门 - Dong Chinese dictionary

evidence.field: 字形演變 字源演變; analysis paragraph
evidence.text: The page presents oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal, clerical, regular, and simplified forms. Its analysis says the graph depicts door pivots and two opposing leaves and calls it an independent pictograph; it contrasts this with Shuowen's parsing as two 戶. It also proposes classifying the graph as 会意 under its own 六書 analysis. This is a conflicting modern classification, not primary paleographic evidence; the database views on pictograph versus two-component analysis are not fully reconciled here.

gaps: Official Unihan character records for U+95E8 and U+9580 were attempted but inaccessible; no local exact kMandarin rows were found. Dong Chinese supplies mén, but official Unihan corroboration remains unverified.
The dossier's sound-related Proto-Sino-Tibetan claim is not applicable to the supported pictographic analysis of 門 and was not independently assessed here. No sound component is proposed for 門.

The evidence supports early gate uses in oracle-bone corpora and later examples, but does not establish a precise earliest semantic extension chronology. The database reports later verbal, metaphorical, and category/lineage senses without dating every transition.

The accounts differ in whether 門 should be called a pictograph or analyzed as composed of two 戶; Shuowen's account is historically important but later than the oracle-bone evidence. The inspected sources do not resolve the graphic classification dispute conclusively.
No glyph images were visually inspected. Graphic comparisons and form labels are paraphrased from the inspected sources.
The source pages describe 门 as the simplified counterpart of 門, but a Unicode or standards source explicitly documenting the standardization relationship was not successfully inspected.
